name: Introduction and overview — Tu-95 Bear — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — Tu-95 Bear
description: Introduction and overview of the Tu-95 Bear: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The Tu-95 Bear is a four-engine turboprop strategic bomber built by Tupolev, entering service in 1956 and still flying. Its swept wings and contra-rotating propellers make it the fastest propeller-driven aircraft ever built. Over 500 were built in bomber, maritime patrol, and reconnaissance versions; the type remains Russia's long-range patrol bomber. Baseline facts: Four-turboprop strategic bomber; service from 1956; 500+ built by Tupolev; still flying..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: Tu-95 Bear: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
